summary.headline: Moneyboxx Q2 FY27 disbursements rose 14% QoQ to ₹87 crore, with October crossing ₹50 crore, while PAT rose to ₹0.9 crore.
summary.overview: Disbursements reached ₹87 crore in Q2 FY27, up 14% sequentially from ₹76 crore in Q1, and monthly run-rate improved from ₹32.4 crore in September to over ₹50 crore in October. Total income was ₹61 crore (up 11% YoY, 17% QoQ) and pre-provision operating profit was ₹9.97 crore (up 79% YoY), with PAT at ₹0.9 crore versus ₹0.28 crore a year earlier. AUM stood at ₹802 crore at September 2026, below the ₹1,057 crore total assets, and management is targeting ₹1,100–1,200 crore AUM by March 2027. Growth is being pursued through four engines (MSME, livestock, rooftop solar, digital lending) with partnership and FLDG-backed structures.

financial_highlights.change: +14% QoQ vs ₹76 crore in Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.value: ₹32.4 crore in September; >₹50 crore in October 2026
financial_highlights.change: More than doubled in two months from ₹24.5 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Net interest income and fee income (Q2)

segments.name: MSME lending (secured and unsecured)
segments.commentary: Core business; secured loans ₹3–30 lakh and unsecured ₹1–3 lakh. Secured book is 73% of AUM; average secured ticket rose to ₹6.7 lakh in Q2 from ₹5.7 lakh in Q1. Branch network of 148 branches across 12 states.

segments.name: Livestock and dairy finance
segments.commentary: Partnership with Akshay Kalpa started in Q2 FY27 with FLDG cover; disbursements only about ₹30 lakh in the first month, with partner handling collections.

segments.name: Rooftop solar finance
segments.commentary: AUM ₹17 crore at September (vs ~₹5.5 crore cited last month); monthly disbursements ₹2.27 crore per the answer, and management targets ₹25 crore per month. Second-loss guarantee of 10% (first loss capped at 3%) and yield of about 22.7–23.5%.

segments.name: Digital small lending (Bachat/True Safe)
segments.commentary: Launched end-September 2026 as lending service provider model with FLDG; about ₹2 crore disbursed in the first period, with ₹5 crore targeted for October.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 internal target: disbursements of ₹500–600 crore, leading to AUM of ₹1,100–1,200 crore by March 2027.
Long-term disbursement goal of ₹100 crore per month; management said it cannot go from ₹15 crore (existing-customer disbursements in October) to ₹100 crore in November.
Medium-term target to bring operating expenses to AUM below 10% within two years (H1 FY27 was 14.3%).
Renewable energy loans targeted at about 10% of AUM over the next year.
Partnership channels: Loom (solar) expected at minimum ₹10 crore per month by January 2027; Bachat digital could reach about ₹20 crore per month from January if it takes off; no firm guidance given.
Management expects lending yields to rise quarter on quarter as existing and higher-profile customers are lent to at higher yields.
capex_capacity: Operations through 148 branches across 12 states as of September 2026, serving about 13,000 live customers.
Moneybox One LOS launched in May 2026; secured file processing time cut to about 6.5–7 days from 10–11 days, and approval to sanction now under 1.5–2 days from about 4 days.
Cattle AI underwriting platform reduces manual screening effort by about 30–40%.
New in-house customer app expected to launch in the coming weeks (November 2026).
Management said investments over the last 18–24 months should now translate into growth, with focus on branch productivity.
demand_pricing: Existing-customer lending restarted in late September 2026 after roughly 18 months of pause post MFI guardrails; ₹15 crore disbursed to this segment in October.
Lending rates: average lending IRR 24.8% in H1; average borrowing IRR 12.7%; NIM 11.9%. Yield moderation attributed to shift to higher-ticket secured book.
Borrowing costs up 25–30 bps in NBFC lending space per management; bank funding expected to stay competitive.
Spread assumptions: about 17–18% on secured loans and about 10% on the other book, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How comfortable is funding, and what is the plan for liability diversification after raising about ₹110 crore in NCDs in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited ₹170 crore of liquidity at end-September, 36 lenders including 12 banks, and NCDs at 46% of borrowings; said funding is not a concern for the next two to three quarters and co-lending/BC is not being used yet.

qa_highlights.question: Are there material regulatory changes expected as a middle-layer NBFC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nothing material is expected beyond some additional compliance requirements.

qa_highlights.question: What are H2 FY27 priorities on AUM, asset quality and profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM growth is the priority, with target disbursements of ₹500–600 crore in H2 and AUM of ₹1,100–1,200 crore; collections improving with NPA collections up since September; profitability is tied to AUM as OPEX is largely fixed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable disbursement run-rate and the expected contribution from partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for ₹100 crore a month eventually; partnerships could contribute ₹90–100 crore per quarter (about ₹30 crore per month) if they scale as expected, but execution risk was flagged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the secured vs unsecured mix and how is it changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Secured is 73% of AUM, down from 87% of Q1 disbursements; mix will shift further as FLDG and guarantee-backed partnerships grow, and unsecured loans are expected to be largely covered by guarantee programs.

qa_highlights.question: What measurable efficiency gains has the Moneybox One technology delivered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited faster file processing, better lead tracking, lower customer acquisition costs versus vendors and a platform able to launch multiple products quickly.

risks_watch: Execution risk on partnership channels (Akshay Kalpa, Bachat, Loom) that management itself flagged as uncertain.
Disbursement momentum must sustain: October's ₹50 crore+ includes only ~₹15 crore from existing customers; the path to ₹500–600 crore in H2 requires a steep ramp.
Yield compression from the shift to secured, higher-ticket lending; NIM and IRR trends need to be tracked quarter on quarter.
Cost of incremental borrowing rising 25–30 bps; funding diversification beyond NCDs and banks still needed.
Reliance on FLDG, first-loss and second-loss guarantee structures for partnership and solar portfolios; quality of these guarantees under stress is untested.
Gap between reported asset quality improvement and the role of ARC transactions; reported 90+ DPD fell to 2.56% from 6.25% partly due to ARC sales.
Path to OPEX/AUM below 10% depends on AUM growing well beyond current ₹802 crore.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on disbursement momentum and new partnerships, but several answers were hedged, with management repeatedly saying targets were internal and execution-dependent. Asset quality and funding were presented as stable, with less detail on the ARC contribution and cost of funds.
key_quotes: So, broadly, we don't see funding as a concern as of now.
So it's a low-o-pics and almost zero credit loss partnership.
The AUM growth is the most important factor, as we see, because our optics is more or less stable now.

adds.what: New in-house customer app (not productive capacity; digital channel)

growth.why: H2 FY27 disbursement target of ₹500–600 crore and AUM of ₹1,100–1,200 crore by March 2027 (vs ₹802 crore in Sept) are backed by monthly run-rate rising to over ₹50 crore in October and four new engines, but no new lending capacity is being added (148 branches unchanged), partner volumes are unconfirmed, and the ₹100 crore/month goal is far off.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects lending yields to rise QoQ as higher-profile customers are lent at higher yields, but H1 NIM was 11.9% with yield moderation from the shift to secured higher-ticket book, and borrowing costs are up 25-30 bps; OPEX at 14.3% of AUM (H1) must fall below 10% to lift margins, which depends on AUM growth.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new lending capacity is being added; branches stay at 148 across 12 states, and management is focusing on productivity of existing branches.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Disbursements rose to ₹87 crore in Q2 (+14% QoQ) and October crossed ₹50 crore, with an internal H2 target of ₹500-600 crore and AUM of ₹1,100-1,200 crore by March 2027 from ₹802 crore, though ~₹15 crore of October was existing-customer lending and partner volumes are unconfirmed.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is not disclosed and capex is not discussed; the growth plan relies on partnerships, FLDG structures and productivity of existing branches rather than new capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: The AUM target of ₹1,100-1,200 crore needs ~37-50% growth in six months from ₹802 crore, and management itself called targets internal and execution-dependent, so an upgrade is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The ₹500-600 crore H2 disbursement target needs a steep ramp from ₹50 crore+ monthly to roughly ₹85-100 crore per month, partnerships flagged as execution-risky (₹90-100 crore per quarter expected), and the ₹100 crore/month goal is far off.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New in-house customer app is expected within weeks (November 2026); Loom solar partnership targeted at minimum ₹10 crore/month by January 2027 and Bachat digital could reach ~₹20 crore/month from January, though no firm guidance.

rows.label: Rooftop solar scale-up toward ₹25 crore/month
rows.why: Solar AUM rose to ₹17 crore at September from ~₹5.5 crore a month earlier and disbursements are ₹2.27 crore/month against a ₹25 crore/month target, so the gap is large and unproven.

rows.label: Opex-to-AUM below 10% within two years
rows.why: H1 FY27 opex was 14.3% of AUM; reaching below 10% requires AUM to grow well beyond ₹802 crore while opex stays largely fixed.

rows.label: Funding cost pressure from borrowing rates
rows.why: Borrowing costs up 25-30 bps across NBFC lending; liquidity is ₹170 crore with 36 lenders and management says funding is not a concern for 2-3 quarters, but diversification beyond NCDs (46% of borrowings) is still needed.

tone.note: Management was confident on the October disbursement run-rate, new partnerships and the Moneybox One tech gains, but hedged that AUM and H2 targets were internal and execution-dependent; analysts probed the path from ₹50 crore to ₹100 crore a month, partnership contribution, and asset-quality and AR
